text:
After a lively season, a short confusion followed staff briefings and the Companion Animal Travel Desk opened the shift with a routine review of carrier labels, pet documents, and handoff notes. Routine work then moved in order through check-in, while the ground team prepared space for careful transfer between services. During this flow, one pet carrier was set on the wrong staging shelf after a document was matched to the wrong folder. The error was found before departure, and the animal was not placed at risk. The traveler remained nearby and was kept informed in calm terms while the desk checked the record again. Maple was one of the pets handled under normal procedures, and the matter was kept contained to the desk area. No distress was noted beyond brief delay and extra verification.

The handling steps were immediate and plain. Staff rechecked the itinerary, compared the tag details against the acceptance form, and corrected the staging location. A second member of staff confirmed the carrier was secure and suitable for transfer. The ground team was advised to pause the handoff until the labels and escort notes matched. After that, the carrier moved onward without further issue, and the traveler proceeded with the journey in the usual manner. The desk also reviewed the nearby files to make sure no other companion animal records had been mixed.

Follow-up actions were completed before the end of the shift. The supervisor reminded staff to keep document folders separate during busy desk work and to verify each carrier against the current record before release. The records aide entered the incident in the daily log and noted no injury, no complaint, and no service failure beyond a brief delay. Aurelia Skyways continues to rely on careful checks at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
